say.text: Final segment. Every question here is new, and the first few have hints; the last ones are a cold check.
Hesselbach's triangle, as the exam key draws it. Which set of borders is correct?

choices.label: Epigastric artery, rectus edge, Cooper's ligament
Epigastric artery, rectus edge, inguinal ligament
Deep inguinal ring, rectus edge, inguinal ligament
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: The deep ring is where the sac enters, but an entry point is not an edge. Rebuild the three sides from what forms the edges.
This is the exam-key set. The sides are the inferior epigastric artery laterally and the rectus sheath edge medially.
The inferior border is the inguinal ligament in exam keys. Older descriptions used Cooper's ligament instead.
Not quite. Cooper's ligament is tempting because older texts used it as the triangle's base.
Exam keys take the inguinal ligament as the inferior border, so Cooper's fails the key.

sure_note.text: You were sure of Cooper's. That is the old base; check the inguinal ligament against the key.

say.text: Not quite. The deep ring is tempting because the sac enters through it.
The ring is an opening in the canal, not an edge of the triangle. Its sides come from the vessels, the rectus edge and the ligament.

sure_note.text: You were sure the ring forms an edge. It is the entry point of an indirect sac, which lies outside the triangle.

say.text: Bedside, after reduction. Patient A's swelling stays away on coughing while you hold the deep ring shut.
Patient B's swelling still comes through, medial to your finger. Which patient has the indirect hernia?

choices.label: Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Your finger blocks the route of a sac that comes through the deep ring. Which sac stays out when that route is shut?
The indirect sac runs through the deep ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. Pressing the ring stops that sac.
Not quite. Patient B seems to fit, since the bulge comes up near the middle of the groin.
A sac that comes through the posterior wall, medial to the epigastric vessels, is direct, and the ring block does not hold it.

sure_note.text: You were sure. Check the route: the indirect sac uses the deep ring, which your finger shuts.

say.text: The invagination test: the little finger pushes the scrotal skin in at the superficial ring.
The impulse is felt on the pulp of the finger, not its tip. Which hernia is it?

choices.label: Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: This test has only two readings, the tip and the pulp. Recall which hernia each part reads.
This is the exam-key reading. An impulse on the tip suggests indirect, and an impulse on the pulp suggests direct.
The pulp reading picks up the direct sac, which comes through the posterior wall.
Not quite. Indirect is tempting because it is the commoner hernia, so it feels like the default.
The finger site decides it. A pulp impulse reads direct, and a tip impulse reads indirect.

sure_note.text: You were sure. The reading comes from the finger site, not from which hernia is common.

say.text: Not quite. Femoral is tempting because it is the ring-finger site in Zieman's test.
The invagination test has only two readings, tip and pulp, and neither is femoral.

sure_note.text: You were sure. Zieman's three-finger test and the invagination test are separate tests with separate readings.

say.text: Take every groin lump seen in women at a surgical clinic.
Which hernia leads that count?

choices.label: Femoral hernia through the femoral canal
Indirect inguinal hernia through the deep ring
Direct inguinal hernia through the posterior wall
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Think about the whole inguinal group first, then the type that leads it in both sexes.
This is the exam-key answer. Indirect inguinal hernia is the most common hernia in women, as it is in men.
Inguinal hernia as a group is the most common abdominal wall hernia in both sexes.
Not quite. Femoral is tempting because it is relatively more common in women than in men.
Relatively is not the same as most common. The leading hernia in women is still the indirect inguinal type.

sure_note.text: You were sure. Femoral is commoner in women, but the leading type in women is still indirect inguinal.

say.text: Close, but not the answer. Direct is an inguinal hernia, so it sits in the right family for this question.
The indirect type is the most common inguinal hernia overall, and it leads in women too.
On ward round a patient asks which inguinal type is more likely to strangulate. What do you tell him?

choices.label: Direct, because its wide bulk can trap the bowel
Indirect, because its deep-ring neck is narrow
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Ask where the sac is squeezed, not how big it is. Which neck is narrower?
This is the exam-key answer. The narrow neck at the deep ring grips the contents, and indirect hernias carry more strangulation risk than direct ones.
Not quite. Bulk is tempting: a big swelling feels like the dangerous one.
Risk follows the neck, not the size. A narrow neck cuts off venous return first, then the arterial supply, and that is strangulation.

sure_note.text: You were sure that bulk decides it. The narrow neck is the danger, not the size of the swelling.

say.text: Cold check from here, with no hints. Ranking groin hernias by strangulation risk, which type sits at the top?

choices.label: Femoral hernia through the femoral canal
Indirect inguinal hernia through the deep ring
Direct inguinal hernia through the posterior wall
Umbilical hernia through the linea alba

say.text: Among groin hernias, the femoral type carries the highest risk of strangulation.
Among the inguinal types, indirect carries more risk than direct.
Not quite. Indirect feels right because it is the commonest inguinal type, and the riskier of the two.
The word 'groin' widens the field to the femoral type, which carries the highest risk of all groin hernias.
Not quite. Direct is tempting because a direct sac bulges forward and feels bulky.
Among the inguinal types the direct sac is the lower-risk one, and among all groin hernias femoral is the most at risk.
Not quite. Umbilical hernias can strangulate, so the choice is tempting.
This ranking covers groin hernias only, and among those the femoral type carries the highest risk.
A 4-year-old boy has a reducible right groin swelling, and his parents ask what operation he needs.
Which operation do you book?

choices.label: Lichtenstein mesh repair of the posterior wall
Herniotomy, high ligation and sac excision

say.text: Herniotomy alone is the paediatric operation: high ligation and excision of the sac.
The defect is a patent processus vaginalis with a normal posterior wall, so the wall needs no repair.
Not quite. Mesh repair is tempting because it is the standard adult open operation.
A child's defect is a patent processus vaginalis with a normal wall, so the adult wall repair does not fit.
Not quite. Herniorrhaphy is tempting because most hernia operations you learn repair the wall.
A child's posterior wall is normal, so a wall repair adds work the defect does not need. Herniorrhaphy is sac excision plus own-tissue repair.
A 60-year-old man has a primary unilateral reducible inguinal hernia, and his unit does open repair only.
Which is the current standard open repair?

choices.label: Bassini repair of the posterior wall
Laparoscopic TEP with mesh behind the sac

say.text: This is the current standard open repair for an adult primary hernia.
Laparoscopy is a good option for primary unilateral hernia in experienced hands, but this unit does open repair.
Not quite. Bassini is tempting because older PYQs gave it as the classic repair.
Current practice uses Lichtenstein mesh for open adult repair. Bassini is the older key.

sure_note.text: You were sure of Bassini. Older keys expected it; the current open standard is Lichtenstein.

say.text: Not quite. Laparoscopy is tempting because it is the newer route with less postoperative pain.
This unit does open repair only, and the primary unilateral qualifier points to open repair with mesh.

sure_note.text: You were sure of laparoscopy. It is preferred for bilateral or recurrent hernias, and for primary ones only in experienced hands.

say.text: A surgeon excises the sac and does nothing to the posterior wall.
What is that operation called?
Herniotomy is excision of the sac, with no repair of the wall.
Herniorrhaphy adds repair with the patient's own tissue, and hernioplasty adds prosthetic mesh.
Not quite. Herniorrhaphy is tempting because the sac is excised here, so it feels like a full repair.
Herniorrhaphy also repairs the posterior wall with the patient's own tissue, and this surgeon does no wall work.
Not quite. Hernioplasty is tempting because mesh is the term many learners remember from modern repairs.
Hernioplasty means reinforcing the wall with prosthetic mesh, and no wall work is done here.
A man had an open repair yesterday. Now he has numbness over the root of the penis, the anterior scrotum and the upper medial thigh.
Which nerve was most likely injured?

choices.label: Ilioinguinal nerve, the sensory nerve of the groin
Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve

say.text: This is the nerve most commonly injured in open repair.
Its territory is the root of the penis, the anterior scrotum and the upper medial thigh.
Not quite. The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is tempting because it is the famous laparoscopic injury.
This man had an open repair, where the nerve hit is the ilioinguinal. The lateral femoral cutaneous is the one hurt in laparoscopy.

sure_note.text: You were sure of the laparoscopic nerve. Match the nerve to the approach that was used.

say.text: Close, but not the classic answer. The genital branch lies in the same field and can be hit.
The question asks for the nerve most commonly injured in open repair, which is the ilioinguinal.
A tack goes in lateral to the gonadal vessels, below the iliopubic tract.
Which triangle is it, and what does it hold?

choices.label: Doom triangle, with the external iliac vessels
Pain triangle, with the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve
Pain triangle, with the external iliac vessels

say.text: This is the triangle of pain, lying lateral to the gonadal vessels.
It contains the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve, the femoral nerve and the femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve.
Not quite. Doom is tempting because both triangles are no-tack zones, and it is the one learners remember.
The doom triangle lies medial to the gonadal vessels, between the vas and them. This tack is lateral to them.
Not quite. The pain triangle is the right triangle, but its contents are nerves, not vessels.
The vessels belong to the doom triangle. The pain triangle holds the lateral femoral cutaneous, femoral and genitofemoral branches.
At an inguinal repair the surgeon finds a Meckel's diverticulum lying in the sac.
Which eponym applies?
Littre's hernia is the one that holds a Meckel's diverticulum.
Amyand's and de Garengeot's hold the appendix, in inguinal and femoral sacs. That is the last check.
Not quite. Amyand's is tempting because the sac holds an inflamed organ, and the appendix comes to mind first.
Amyand's is an appendix in an inguinal sac. This sac holds a Meckel's diverticulum, so the content fails.
Not quite. De Garengeot is tempting because it is also a named organ-in-sac hernia.
De Garengeot is an appendix in a femoral sac. This sac holds a Meckel's diverticulum, so the organ and the site both fail.

cards.q: Which sides and base make up Hesselbach's triangle in exam keys?
cards.a: Inferior epigastric artery laterally, rectus sheath edge medially, and the inguinal ligament inferiorly. Cooper's ligament was the older base.

cards.q: Which hernia is most common in women?
cards.a: Indirect inguinal hernia, the leading type in women as in men. Inguinal hernia is the most common abdominal wall hernia in both sexes.

cards.q: Which groin hernia is most likely to strangulate?
cards.a: Femoral hernia. Among inguinal types, indirect carries more risk than direct.

cards.q: Which operation for a child's inguinal hernia, and which open adult repair is current?
cards.a: Herniotomy alone in children, with no wall repair. Lichtenstein mesh is the adult open standard; Bassini is the older key.

cards.q: Which nerve is most commonly injured in open repair, and which in laparoscopic repair?
cards.a: Ilioinguinal in open repair; lateral femoral cutaneous in laparoscopic repair.
